Getting Started
This demo app showcases OpenTelemetry mobile observability patterns. Use the scenario buttons to generate telemetry events and see how they're buffered and exported to an OpenTelemetry Collector.
Demo Scenarios
Scenario A: UI Freeze Detection

Simulates a 2.5 second UI freeze on the main thread. This generates user activity events followed by a ui.freeze event with duration_ms > 2000, which should trigger an export policy to flush the last 2 minutes of buffered events.
Scenario B: Crash Simulation

Marks a crash flag and generates background task events. On the next app start, the crash will be detected and a crash recovery policy will flush the last 5 minutes from disk buffer, providing historical context for the crash.
Scenario C: Network Error

Simulates successful API calls followed by an HTTP 500 error. This should trigger an export policy that flushes recent events and increases sampling rate to 100% for 10 minutes to capture more context during the incident.
Force Flush

Manually triggers an immediate export of all buffered events (both RAM and disk). If no collector is running, you'll see retry attempts with exponential backoff. Events remain safely buffered until the collector becomes available.

Use the Settings menu to configure:

• Protocol: gRPC (binary/fast) or HTTP (JSON/compatible)
• Collector endpoint
• Authorization token (Bearer auth - required for both protocols)
• Dataset/Tenant ID (for multi-tenant backends)
• Buffer sizes (RAM: 5000 events, Disk: 50MB)
• Retry behavior (max retries, timeout)
• Context enrichment (geo/device attributes)

Changes require an app restart to take effect.
Protocol Selection

gRPC (Recommended):
• Binary Protobuf encoding for efficiency
• Lower latency and better performance
• Single endpoint for all signals (logs, traces, metrics)
• Port 4317 by default
• Example: https://ingress.dash0.com:4317
• Authentication: Same Bearer token in metadata

HTTP:
• JSON encoding for compatibility
• Better firewall/proxy support
• Separate path per signal (/v1/logs, /v1/traces, /v1/metrics)
• Standard HTTPS port (443)
• Example: https://ingress.dash0.com/v1/logs
• Authentication: Same Bearer token in HTTP headers

Both protocols use identical authentication (Authorization: Bearer token).

For cloud-based collectors that require authentication:

1. Get your auth token from your observability provider
2. Go to Settings → Authorization Token
3. Enter your token (e.g., auth_fI0GuunaYYbw8u0n0iyFAC4Wt2FMf0jh)
4. If using a multi-tenant backend, enter your Dataset/Tenant ID
5. Save and restart the app

The app will automatically add 'Authorization: Bearer [token]' and 'Dash0-Dataset: [dataset]' headers to all OTLP requests.

Offline Resilience

The app handles various failure scenarios:

• Network loss: Events queue in RAM and disk buffers
• App crash: Disk buffer survives, auto-detected on restart
• Collector down: Retry with exponential backoff (1s → 2s → 4s → 8s)
• Extended outage: Disk buffer holds events for up to 24 hours (configurable TTL)

Events are never lost as long as disk space is available.

Export failures are expected if no collector is running. To test with a real collector:

1. Start an OTEL Collector on your machine (port 8080)
2. Update the collector endpoint in Settings
3. Restart the app
4. Run scenarios and verify telemetry in your backend

For Android emulator, use http://10.0.2.2:8080 to reach localhost on your machine.
